Tonight, Thursday Night Football has the 0-4 Bucs at Dallas. Your Tech Demo: record a task once and get a finished step-by-step guide. fall down 7 stand up 8.

openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Cool clear air, Jupiter's day. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Wide chest, slow pulse, open hands. Launch days reward the person who is calm at 11:10 — that's you.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the rest of the board.

mindset.body: Jupiter is the planet of growth, kingship and generosity — the big-picture planet. Today Dom doesn't play small. You built the page, you set the window, and at 11:11 the door opens. You don't chase, you don't refresh, you don't flinch. You show up like the offer is already worth it, because it is. Competitive. Unbeatable. One breath, one launch, one clean finish. fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Thursday: run this right after Morning Charge — breath first, then the body. 49° and clear outside; get warm before the screens. Then news and the pre-launch check.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

items.hed: OpenAI posts 722 math papers from an unreleased model
items.body: The batch spans about 20 fields, including more than 80 theoretical-CS papers and work on the Navier–Stokes equations; many include Lean files so a computer can check the proof. Mathematicians are impressed and a little baffled by the volume, and want the model name and prompts disclosed.

items.hed: Grok Bot will route work to Claude Opus 5.5, Midjourney and Suno
items.body: Musk said SpaceX will use 'the best back end model for any given task,' including Anthropic's latest Claude, rather than only its own Grok models. He didn't say which jobs go where. It's a boost for Anthropic ahead of its expected IPO.

items.hed: Apple may need an official off switch for Apple Intelligence on Macs
items.body: The latest models can take up to 14GB, and an unofficial tool called RemoveMacAI is spreading. Organizations that ban AI tools want one switch to turn it all off and delete the models, which Apple doesn't offer yet.

items.hed: Dana White starts selling Fury–Joshua tickets anyway
items.body: White posted a ticket promo Wednesday morning, beating Eddie Hearn's own announcement by 13 minutes. Tickets for the Dec 11 Cardiff fight go on sale Friday at 6:00 AM CT; Hearn still says Joshua's contract bars White from promoting.

items.hed: Hearn: the UFC 'is under threat right now'
items.body: Hearn says White's focus on Zuffa Boxing is costing the UFC, citing a lack of stars and new competitors lining up. Next up on the UFC calendar: Allen vs Duncan this Saturday in Vegas.

In the old planetary week Thursday is Jupiter's day — jeudi in French, jueves in Spanish. English named it for Thor, the thunder god, the Norse match for Jupiter's lightning. Jupiter rules growth, generosity, rulership and good fortune. It's the day for the big ask and the bold launch.

The Solomonic grimoires, including the Key of Solomon, teach planetary hours: each day's first hour after sunrise belongs to that day's planet. Today's Jupiter hour starts at sunrise, 6:57 AM in Carpentersville. Magicians saved that hour for work meant to grow — a good time to set the intention for your launch.

On the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, Jupiter sits at Chesed, 'loving-kindness,' the sphere of expansion and giving. Its partner across the tree is Geburah (Mars), strength and limits. The teaching: growth without structure spills, and structure without growth starves. A 24-hour window with a hard close is both.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.source: From the wisdom attributed to Solomon
grimoire.hed: Commit the work, and the thoughts are established
grimoire.body: Solomon's proverb: 'Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established' (Proverbs 16:3). The order matters. You don't wait for your thoughts to settle before you act — you commit the work, and the steadiness follows. On Jupiter's day, with a window opening at 11:11, the teaching is simple: hand the outcome over, do your part cleanly, and let your mind go quiet because the work is already set in motion.
grimoire.practice: After four rounds of box breathing, say out loud: 'The work is committed. The window is open.' Do your pre-launch check once, completely, then close the tab. Don't refresh until the midpoint. Then start the 3-minute opener.

lesson.oneLiner: Do a task once with a step-recorder running, and you get a finished how-to guide without writing it.
beats: Do it: start the recorder (Scribe runs as a browser extension or desktop app), then do the task the normal way.
Capture: every click and keystroke becomes a numbered step with a screenshot attached, so nobody has to guess what 'go to settings' means.
Ship: trim the extra steps, add one tip where people usually get stuck, and export it as a PDF or a share link.
Use it: that's an SOP for work (the payoff-request workflow is the perfect first one) or the skeleton of a 7EightMade PDF drop.
lesson.takeaway: Show, don't write. @mmmik000: the fastest way to document a process is to do it once while something watches.
